newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SETS RULES TO BOOST GVT SECURITIES TRADING.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SETS RULES TO BOOST GVT SECURITIES TRADING.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) has issued new rules to set up a framework for primary and secondary markets in government securities and make trading more active, a BNR official said on Thursday.
"We aim to enhance trading on the secondary market," BNR general manager George Mucibabici told Reuters.

"With an active and fluid secondary market of government securities, (our) next step will be shifting to open-market operations and replacing current refinancing auctions with repurchase agreements (repos)."

Under the new rules, banks and financial institutions operating in Romania can be licensed as primary dealers provided they meet requirements, including an account with the BNR, a minimum capital -- yet to be decided -- and a minimum performance on the primary market.
The BNR rules also stipulate that individuals or companies may be accepted as primary market participants, but makes no specific reference to the access of foreigners to the market.
Local bankers said foreigners' access would be regulated through a portfolio investment bill or amendments to the public debt law to be discussed soon by parliament.
"This will become one of the hottest local markets in the region after Russia," a London analyst said by telephone.
The rules also introduce new procedures, such as auctions in addition to the current public subscriptions, for placing the government papers to make the primary market more flexible.
A primary dealer will submit bids for a minimum part of each new issue and also underwrite it, maintain quotes in benchmark issues and have "a minimum activity on the secondary market".
Initially around 30 banks will operate as primary dealers. The BNR will then select a class of primary dealers which also might include securities companies.
Settlements would be carried out by the BNR, which registers the papers' holders and supervises state securities markets.
The first pilot operations under the new regulation will take place next week when the ministry will issue rollover 91-day treasury bills to cover maturing papers.
Romania has so far funded the bulk of its budget deficits through treasury bills, most on short-term, pressing the finance ministry to launch several rollover issues.

With an almost absent secondary market, the ministry had to offer high yields to secure bills' placement through the BNR. The total of outstanding domestic bills amounts to 4.2 trillion lei. Internal public debt was 6.69 trillion lei at end-1996.
Secondary market turnover was 2.13 billion lei in March, but trading livened up this month with falling money market rates making investments in fixed-coupon T-bills attractive.
Last week, the ministry's T-bill offer in a public subscription was heavily oversubscribed with yield at 193.22 percent compared with short-term money market prices of 105. ($=7,063 lei) REUTER
